items.heading: EDITORIAL
items.summary: Editorial praising the club's young athletes - the girls' walking team, Joann Warnett, Richard Dorman, the Youth cross country team and Mark Shippen - and the three men who organise them, Carl Lawton, Ray Hall and Leo Coy, urging members to take an interest in the youngsters.
items.text:
How heartening it is to see our youngsters pushing the name of our Club to the fore.

Only eighteen months after the first girls joined Belgrave Harriers the signs are that we have the fastest improving ladies walking team in the country. The great thing is that they become stronger with every week that passes and all have youth on their side. Whilst most of our lady walkers have already made their names well known to us through their deeds on road and track it must be mentioned that another lass, fourteen year old Joann Warnett, is also making a name for herself in the world of cross country running, winning the Wandsworth Schools event, finishing highly placed in the Greater London Schools race and gaining selection to run in the All England Schools Championship.

Do not imagine, however, that our young men are letting the ladies have the stage to themselves. Junior Captain Richard Dorman leads by example and this past winter season has seen him develop into a fine walker, already making his presence felt among the seniors, and as our leading Youth cross country runner has brought the Bels to victory in their Surrey C.C. League events. The cross country team that followed Richard is being viewed with great interest as well, for all still remain Youths next winter.

With the summer season now approaching it will be interesting to see how Mark Shippen continues his progress in the pole vault. Last year while still a youth he ranked =22nd in the Nation's Senior list and 5th among the Juniors. And of course there are quite a few others - jumpers, throwers and runners - who have also already made their mark in Senior competition while still teenagers and who should be ready to improve again with another winter under their belts.

This progress has not come about by pure chance. Three men have put a great deal of their time and energy into organising our young teams' training and competition - Carl Lawton (walking), Ray Hall (Ladies cross country, track and field) and Leo Coy (Youths and Boys). Their tasks can be counted perhaps the most rewarding in our sport;
continued at the foot of page 5.

EDITORIAL .... continued from page 3.
helping the development of young athletes on the way up. On the other hand they are most certainly at the same time the most heartbreaking when things are not going well and when the general membership shows little or no interest in what they are trying to do and offering them no help with their efforts. Need we say more!

One way in which all members can help is simply by taking notice. Ask our youngsters how their training is going, when will they be competing next, how did they get on last time. It means a great deal to be noticed by those who "matter".

items.heading: grapevine
items.summary: Grapevine club news column: members abroad (Stuart Masterson, Graham Seatter, Allan Callow, John Knifton), births, Charlie Speechley's 90th birthday, Bernard Eglington's retirement, Cyril Gittins' R.W.A. presidency, Don Maclean's darts win, the club's 1977 membership figures and other notes.
items.text:
grapevine

Stuart Masterson has returned to Australian for a couple of years; let us hope that we have not seen the last of this friendly road runner. Stuart would be more than pleased to hear how his old colleagues are getting on so why not drop him a line - 56 Birtwistle Plac[illegible] Poleystone 6111, Western Australia.

We are also very sad to see the return to New Zealand of Graham Seatter but hopefully we will be able to see him in action later this year via our TV screens when the Commonwealth Games at Edmonton, Canada, take place. Graham made many friends while over here - walke[illegible] and road runners - and this is one of the great things about our spor[illegible] our common interest in athletics that serves as a basis to meet and enjoy the company of folk of all nationalities, from all walks of life

However, another Belgravian is planning to return to the UK this summer - Allan Callow. Allan, a past committee member of our club has enjoyed a deal of success while in New Zealand. On October 8th he won an over distance 20 mile Walk at Dunedin beating the NZ 50Km Champion John Rayner in the process, having set a pb of 36:03 for 5 miles the previous week.

Many congratulations to Carl and Barbara Lawton on the birth of son Colin, who arrived on October 23rd weighing 7lb 12oz. And while on the subject of prospective members we must also welcome Faye, daughter of Bernard and Margaret Merry, who was born in December

Charlie Speechley recently received a 90th Birthday Card signed by the President and a number of members. He also received a presentation plaque from the Veterans A.C. He was at the Murphy Shield (10 miles walk) Race and was soon chatting to old friends. He also made the acquaintance of our youngest member, Colin Lawton - 90 years between them!

Surrey County Womens' A.A.A. soon took advantage of our facilities for the ladies. They held their cross country championships there in December. In charge of the proceedings was Win. Shepherd with a number of members helping in the background. We were pleased to hear that Past President of the Assn., Mrs Savage (Win's mother) is still about and enjoying life at eighty plus.

The Boxing Day Meeting usually attracts the odd older member and this year it was F.A. (Mick) Walker, cross country and road runner of the thirties and forties. He scored in a number of Surrey County Championship wins, but he was perhaps best known for his runs at 20 miles and the marathon (nothing longer in those days). During World War II he won the Finchley '20'. He has lived in Cornwall for a number of years.

John Knifton writes from Austin (Texas) where it is much hotter than it is here. Because of the heat he trains late in the evening but even so it is still too hot for speed work. Consequently when he goes to a cooler place for a race (some hundreds of miles away in many cases) the lack of speed work plus Anno Domini begins to tell. However it is good to see his name occasionally in the U.S.A. results. He hopes to visit the U.K. in 1979 - give him a number Carl!

Bernard Eglington informs us that he is retiring this year. He will be cutting down on his forays into Lancashire for the occasional spin. He plans to keep his tracksuit aired regularly on the front at Colwyn Bay. When he first joined us he was a runner with the R.A.F. (he also sported a Derby & County Vest). He switched to walking and soon became a regular member of our teams at all distances gaining a number of winning and place medals.

Merton Schools' have a nice muddy cross country course from their sports ground at Beverley Meads (hard by Beverley Brook and the woods at the foot of Wimbledon Common). A number of Belgravians were representing their schools at this year's championships; star of the meeting was Richard Dorman, Raynes Park High School, who not only won the race for the oldest age group but set a new course record.

Warmest congratulations to our Q.P.H. member, Cyril Gittins, upon being elected President of the Southern Area of the R.W.A. Cyril has also had a spell in the Chair, is a Grade I Timekeeper, and is a regular official at our Battersea Park meetings. A "back-room boy" whose continued service makes our sport possible.

You should have seen them ... past champions Arthur Penny and Tom Carter showing each other their pensioners bus passes while waiting for the runners to reappear after the first lap of our cross country course. We won't insult them by saying how spritely and fit they look, as we know full well that the only reason they don't don a pair of shorts each and set out with the competitors is that they might embarrass the Club by getting among the scorers again!

Meanwhile, one of their peers, Harry Shields, always searching for another cultural pursuit, has taught himself to paint by attending evening classes, and we are pleased to say that some of Harry's work was recently on exhibition. What talent we have in the Club.

Well done Don Maclean, who has managed to get his name on the "Denmark Pot" by winning our Darts Championship. It is particularly appropriate that Don should win this event at last for he was one of its instigators some dozen or so years ago.

At the end of 1977 the total strength of Belgrave Harriers stood at 563 members - 494 men (278 Seniors, 30 Juniors, 26 Youths, 107 Boys, 25 Associate Members, 7 Honorary Members and 21 Second-claim Members) and 69 women (9 Seniors, 6 Juniors, 49 Girls, 2 Associate Members and 3 Second-claim Members).

items.heading: WALKING
items.summary: Walking secretary's review: the ladies' team fifth in the National Women's 5Km, new recruits Shirley Rook and Linda Nicholls, the men's teams in the National rankings and junior championships, and tributes to Graham Seatter, Ray Middleton and John Hall.
items.text:
WALKING

National Medals for a Belgrave Ladies Team. - Not an impossible dream but almost a reality. In the National Women's 5Kms walk championship at Birmingham in December we finished 5th only 7 points from 2nd place and that was with the misfortune of a disqualification without which we would have been placed.

Since the last edition we have increased our ladies section by a sufficient number to give us a team to be reckoned with. It took eighteen months to gently suggest to Shirley Rook that it would be the best policy for her to join us and eventually she made her decision and is now our number 1. Also joining us recently was Linda Nicholls who will be able to compete in the team in a few months. (She was quickly followed by her brother Michael).

As to the men - 2nd overall in the National rankings - we would have won it had we started a Youths team in '76. But this year we have already started off on the wrong foot. The National, Junior, Youths and Boys at Wimbledon, was the first time that the Boys championship was to be included in the tables. Fortunately we just started a boy[illegible] team but not the team it should have been and we finished last. In the Youths we did not start a team although one was entered. Fourth in the Juniors was the best we could do with what we had but if.....
Thanks are extended to all who turned up to help make the event a success.

Graham Seatter has returned home and will leave a gap difficult to fill. He managed to fit into 12 months what most of us would do in three years. He arrived as a "useful" walker, he went through bad spells, foot injury, anaemia, a hospital operation, had holidays in Scotland, Ireland, Cornwall and the Isle of Man but still managed to win the National Junior, Leicester 7, Lambeth 10Kms, Enfield 20Km[illegible] and finally his parting triumph the Belgrave 7 and of course he was part of the many Belgrave team victories during the year.

One of the dangers of signing a new walker who will immediately fill a team place is that he will push out one of the old brigade. This method has been tried for years but Ray Middleton still comes back!! Always a stalwart, always there in the Open team wins, and first man in the National 50Kms, Hastings and Brighton.

John Hall is a hard worker who arrived on the Belgrave scene in 1971 as an average mid field man. Over the years he trained, he raced and slowly improved, then '77 was the year that he made the grade. Six years to get there but now, in the first 10 in the opens, an equivalent of sub 52 minutes for 7 miles in the 11Kms at Imber Court, a sub 70 minutes 15Kms and then the Sussex 10 miles title in '78. He also did the Hastings and beat a few notable distance men.

Looking to 1978, well by the time you read this the National 10 will have passed by. National Titles are not impossible but............ There is always a team placed to be filled - Bob Picton at Highgate, Jon Dunsford at Luton, Richard Dorman (in his first outing as a team member) at Imber Court. We have a few new faces in the club and the future is rosy if the backing can be provided - a turn out of four starters in the 50 kilos will not win the team of eight!

Carl Lawton, Walking Hon. Secretary.

items.summary: Walking reports from August 1977: Belgrave team wins in the Hastings to Brighton and the Lambeth Festival of Race Walking, Carl Lawton's South Western Counties 10Km win, and Graham Seatter's records at the London Vidarians 5 miles and the Enfield 20Km.
items.text:
On August 6th Belgrave again took the Hastings to Brighton event thanks to the trio of Ray Middleton (4th 5:42:37), John Hall (8th 6:03:33) and Carl Lawton (15th 6:16:19). Alain Moulinet of France won the event, the 40th time it has been held, in 5:34:54. The pace had been fast throughout with 50Km coming up for our men in 4:34:55, 4:52:55 and 5:54:24. Dave King and John Keown also competed for the Bels whose score of 17 points was 6 points too good for second placers Brighton & Hove.

One week later came a sparkling 1 - 2 from Graham Seatter and Carl Lawton in the Lambeth Festival of Race Walking at Brockwell Park. Graham had just over half a minute on Carl at the finish of the 10Km. 44:43 to 45:15, with Amos Seddon (BoE) a further five seconds down. Other Belgrave placings were: 10.J.Hall 48:06; 15.R.Middleton 48:59; 26.J.Dunsford 53:08; 34.R.Day 54:36; 37.D.Fotheringham 55:31; 42.S. Bennett 56:32; 52.J.Morris 59:59. Once again the team race went to the Bels with 12 points to Brighton & Hove's 23 and Boro' of Enfield's 24.

In the Youth's 5Km at Lambeth Richard Dorman placed 6th in 25:49 with T.McDermot and P.Morris also competing. Diane Cook was third home in the Women's 10Km and Jane Pritchard was in action in the intermediate girls 5Km.

August 20th saw Carl successfully tackling the South Western Counties 10Km at Weymouth, winning in 46:46, while over the London Vidarians 5 mile course Graham Seatter zipped to a record 34:59.

The fearsome conditions did not deter Graham Seatter from blazing from start to finish to win the Enfield 20Km on August 28th. At 10Km he was timed at 44:30, over a minute up on Seddon, and in torrential rain he drew even further away to set a new personal best of 91:01. Ray Middleton was 15th in 100:37 with Doug. Fotheringham also in the field but Carl had to retire due to back trouble. In the womens 5Km Anna Matthews placed 5th in 30:53 and Jane Pritchard 7th in 32:40.

items.heading: SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON. LEICESTER'S TURN!
items.summary: Report by G.S.D. of the 1977 London to Brighton walk, won by John Lees of Brighton & Hove, with Leicester taking the team title and Belgrave second (Ray Middleton fourth), plus a Belgrave 1-2-3 in the G.L.C. Championships 3Km.
items.text:
SEPTEMBER 3rd 1977 - LONDON TO BRIGHTON.
LEICESTER'S TURN!

This year saw 69 starters in the Open London to Brighton Walk, five of whom were ours. The weather was kind, a little breeze and a little sun but no rain. In the early stages Ray was with the leaders with Dave and Ron walking together not too far down the field. The two Johns completed our team and, if all went well, one of these would be our fourth scorer. By twenty miles Ray had lost a few minutes on the leaders who were moving very well. About halfway John Morris retired; our remaining four were still going strong. Dave was able to open up a gap on Ron (suffering the effects of a recent cold) but Ron always had Dave in sight on the long stretches - it's always good to have someone in view on these long efforts!

Thus the race had developed and history was made when John Lees became the first Brighton walker to win this event, his time of 7h.54m. 52s being very good indeed. He was well ahead of Alan Moulinet the Frenchman who had won the Hastings to Brighton a few weeks earlier. Ray was beaten into fourth place by Ken Harding (Royal Sutton Coldfield) who this year broke Pat Duncan's Manchester to Blackpool record. Soon the blue vests of Leicester came rolling in and they had three men home before our second man, Dave, came in and before Ron came in a fourth Leicester man appeared to give them the team title. Congratulations to Leicester who won the race thirty years ago. The battle for placings in the team race was now on, Ron soon came in followed by a Brighton man and with three men home from each team Brighton had a two points advantage. A stolid John Keown arrived four places ahead of our rivals and so we took second medals. This was John's 17th consecutive Brighton!

Thanks again to the usual band of helpers, particularly Richard Dorman who cycled down.
G.S.D.

1.J.Lees (Brighton & Hove) 7:54:52; 4.R.Middleton 8:23:45; 16.D.King 9:18:54; 20.R.Day 9:23:28; 33.J.Keown 9:53:22.
Teams: 1.Leicester WC 28; 2.Belgrave H 42; 3.Brighton & Hove AC 44.

Meanwhile, over at West London Stadium for the G.L.C. Championships, it was Belgrave 1-2-3 as Graham Seatter 12:33, Carl Lawton 13:05 and John Hall 13:12.8 swept the board in the 3Km.

items.text:
SEPTEMBER 10th 1977 - SOUTHWICK - SOUTHERN R.W.A. CHAMPS.

A week after the London to Brighton Walk a small band of Belgravians made the trip to Southwick on the Western suburbs of Brighton for the Southern RWA Juniors, Youths and Boys Championship. The course was based on the Green which is almost exactly 1,000 metres around. Our sole representative in the Boys 3,000m was Kevin McDermot, a newcomer who clocked a creditable 17:11 for 17th. Kevin and his brother Trevor look tough and strong and are training with Ray Middleton who lives nearby - those Hendon roads will soon need re-surfacing. The Youth's 5,000m gave us our best result with Richard Dorman taking second place to Gordon Vale (Surrey W.C.) in 25:13. The aforementioned Trevor was 11th in 26:44 with Peter Morris 18th in 28:37. When Richard becomes eligible to represent us we should have a good team. In the 10,000m Junior Nigel Morris 20th in 56:06 and Stu Bennett 11th in 57:38 were obviously not at their best but worked hard against the odds.
G.S.D.

John Hall's pb for 3,000 metres took another dive on September 14th at Crystal Palace when he clocked 13:04 for 5th. The event was the Southern 3Km championship won by Lightman (Met WC) in 12:40, although first to cross the line was guest Canadian Marcel Jobin in 12:23.6. Carl Lawton placed 3rd in the championship with 12:45.0 while Jonathon Dunsford 14:05 and Ron Day 14:28 also competed.

items.heading: NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - ENFIELD. DOUBLE EVENT
items.summary: Report and results of the Enfield Open 7 miles walk meeting, where Belgrave won the men's team race and the girls won the senior women's 5,000 metres team race.
items.text:
NOVEMBER 12th 1977 - ENFIELD.
DOUBLE EVENT

On November 12th Club history was made at Enfield for not only did we notch up another scratch team in their 54th Open 7 miles walk but our girls won the team race in the Senior over fifteen 5,000 metres. The meeting comprised five events and we were represented in four of them.

Taking the afternoon's events in order, first the Girls (11-15)2,500m and amongst those lined up was Tracey McDermot. This was her first race and wisely she let the more experienced ones go away, nevertheless she persevered with a fine style and with more experience is going to be challenging the others.

Next the Senior Women's 5,000m which turned out to be between Epsom and ourselves. Anna soon established herself with the leaders with Diane not too far behind and Jane putting up her usual fight to keep us in contention. With vocal support our trio maintained their positions to give us a one point victory. Congratulations to them - may this be the first of many.

Meanwhile the Boys (13-15) 5,000, had got under way and Kevin McDermot was already making his presence felt, but as the race progressed some of his speedier rivals pulled away, but he showed his fighting qualities to bring out a personal best.

The main event, the 7 miles saw the Mexican E.Vera in action, for two of the three laps he led Bob Dobson (Southend), but on the third lap he was away on his own to finish in 48:44 with Dobson second. Easily the best of the remainder was Graham, whilst Carl was showing young Colin what its' all about (he slept through the proceedings). John was in good form and soon appeared and it was not long before Ray came in to give us another team win.

Shortly before the hour was up Trevor McDermott crossed the line - only 16 years of age and '7 in the hour' in his first season. Trevor and Kevin are both strong with good styles and are training under the eye of the old master himself, Ray Middleton. Another improving youngster showing his paces was Peter Morris who is showing some of the Seniors a clean pair of heels.

items.heading: NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN '7'. BON VOYAGE !
items.summary: Report and results of the 58th Belgrave Open Seven Miles Walk at Wimbledon, won by New Zealander Graham Seatter in his last walk before returning home, with notes on the club officials and on Havering AC's walks the next day.
items.text:
NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE OPEN '7'.
BON VOYAGE !

The 58th Open Seven Miles Walk was once again a triumph of Belgrave organisation and Belgrave walking tinged however with some regret as our popular New Zealander, Graham Seatter was due to leave for home the following Monday. There was general pleasure that his last walk for us (for a while) brought him a fine win over the Sheffield 50 Kilos specialist, Jake Warhurst. With Carl and John (who nearly caught him) finishing in good positions and with Ray giving his usual support we held off a strong challenge from Steyning, now a strong force to be reckoned with. We had the usual backing of non-scorers and for the first time four of our ladies took to the road (unofficially of course!) and Shirley, Anna, Diane and Jane impressed us all by their determined walking.

There was the usual crowd of Bels doing their jobs, headed by our President who was Starter and Referee. Amongst the Judges were Joe Coleman, Fred Denny, Barbara Dunsford, Harold King, Syd Spencer, Bill True and Joe Wilson. Ray Hall together with Fred and Bill were logging them in, the sheets going in to Jack Goswell and Frank Jarvis, assisted by their wives to get out the results. Also seen on the course were Charlie Churcher, Charlie Jones, Tommy Scrimshaw, Frank Webb, Norman Dewberry and Charlie MacLennan.

Tommy Cook's wife, assisted by other ladies dealt with refreshments. The whole of the proceedings were masterminded by Carl and once again our thanks and full marks to him.

It is fitting to close by wishing Graham and the charming Rosemary "Au Revoir" we hope that you enjoyed your visit to the U.K. as much as we enjoyed your company. Good Luck with your walking in New Zealand and may you soon be back in the Claret and Gold of Belgrave.

items.heading: DECEMBER 31st 1977 - WIMBLEDON - HORWOOD CUP '7'. AGONY CORNER
items.summary: Report and results of the Horwood Cup seven miles walk on a new hilly Wimbledon course planned by Carl, won by Richard Dorman, with matches against the Metropolitan Police and Combined Clubs.
items.text:
DECEMBER 31st 1977 - WIMBLEDON - HORWOOD CUP '7'.
AGONY CORNER

Does such a place exist? Ask any of those who competed in our Seven Miles Walk on December 31st using a new course, where a sharp hill up Cottenham Drive had to be climbed three times. The villain of the piece, the chap who planned it, was Carl, seeking out an alternative for the traditional Open Seven course which is getting dangerous in parts. It was agreed that the new course was better from the safety angle, and, in retrospect, the competitors liked it.

Being the Season of Goodwill we welcomed a number of walkers from other Clubs and we were able to provide matches against the Metropolitan Police and against Combined Clubs.

Carl was directing the competitors round an innocent looking corner where the climbing began. Sweeping round in fine style Adrian James (Enfield) led them home to set a course record of 54:21. Our main interest was in the Horwood Cup for those not barred from the Garnet Trophy and Richard Dorman, improving every time won from Trevor Mc Dermot, also making good progress. (These two gave further evidence of their prowess the following week-end at Imber Court).

We beat the M.P. by a narrow margin, but the Combined Clubs were too strong for us. Many will look forward to improving these times, whilst others will be anxious to have a go on the new course.

items.text:
JANUARY 8th 1978 - IMBER COURT - MET. POLICE OPEN 11KM.
RICHARD'S FINE DEBUT

With the departure of Graham Seatter back to New Zealand, who would fill the gap in our team? The answer came in the Metropolitan Police Open 11 Kilos walk. Sixteen years old Richard Dorman, who the previous day had run so well in the Surrey County C.C. Championships gave us an unprecedented performance. In his first Open race at this distance he was fourth scorer in our team which placed second to the much improved Steyning A.C.

John led the team home with what was probably his best open placing to date, he was near the leaders right from the start. Carl soon followed with Ray, who had had Richard for company in the early stages, hammering his way home. It wasn't long before Richard obliged with a performance which, had the course been seven miles, must have brought him home under the hour. Young Trevor too, who has already done seven miles in the hour, consolidated his position as one of our good prospects.

There were many Belgravians in the field and those trying to make the team can't relax! We welcomed Len Duquemin back to the fray, his style is still very impressive, and a few more outings should bring the speed back.

The event was once again efficiently organised by Doug Fotheringham (who also competed) and it is an event where one often meets old friends. Usually helping at this event is Mrs. Bonnie Yescombe, and she asked after many Club members. Many will recall her late husband Cyril's purposeful walking for Club and Police teams. One of his greatest performances was when in almost continuous raid he walked from Brighton to London and back step for step with Bernard Eglinton

items.summary: Report and results of the G.L.C. 10 miles walking championship at Battersea Park, won by G. Nibre of Ilford, where Belgrave finished second team by one point between Ilford and Enfield.
items.text:
FEBRUARY 11th, 1978 - BATTERSEA PARK - G.L.C. 10 MILE CHAMPIONSHIP.
34—35—36

These were the team scores in this year's G.L.C. 10 miles Walking Championship of Ilford AC (without Roger Mills), Belgrave and Enfield (without Amos Seddon), with Surrey WC not far behind with 42 points.

The event was held at Battersea Park on the 11th February over the usual five lap course; it was dry but cold.

Carl and John Hall were prominent in the early stages and Surrey WC seemed to have the edge over us for the team title, but Ray and John Bromley were moving well. The winner, who led for most of the way, was G. Nibre of Ilford - one of the country's promising young walkers. With a lap to go Carl and S. Elms (Sutton) were in hot pursuit, but over the last lap the diminutive Brighton man put in some fast work to drop Carl. John kept up the pressure and recorded a time equivalent to eight m.p.h. Ray and John were picking up places and it was good to see how their judgment and experience got them really moving over that part of the race which matters.

The closeness of the result shows how tight team races are these days, actually we were the first club to finish its four scorers. It was good to see John Dunsford and Ron Day getting back to form.

WITH THE LADIES

The Ladies Section, from the point of competition, goes into hibernation for the Winter at present, but the track training with 18-20 youngsters still goes on at Battersea Park every Sunday morning throughout the Winter, and every Wednesday evening at Belgrave Hall with circuit training and games.

Our Walkers, however, have competed in three major championships, the first being the National Junior 5000m at Milksham in November, where Diane Cook finished 6th in her first championship race for the Club and Anna Matthews was unfortunately disqualified while fighting out for 3rd place. The National Championships came next, and were held at Birmingham on a Sunday early in December, where Belgrave fielded a full team in the Senior section for the first time in history. The last championship was the Southern Counties at Maidstone and this race saw the first appearance of Linda Nicholls, the Kent Champion, in Belgrave colours. Welcome Linda, you've got your worst race out of your system, and it was a horrid day.

Looking further forward it can only be a matter of months before our walking team gains Championship medals, and my thanks go to Carl Lawton for providing transport and support for the Birmingham trip.

★★★

For full details of walking events see under The Walking Section.

We held our Cross Country Championships at Wimbledon on January 21st. The Junior race had eight competitors and Joann Warnett won comfortably with the Taylor sisters second and third. Rebecca Augustine and Alison Jones surprised with their forward running. The Senior race saw Shirley Rook winning easily, her first Club Championship, from Anna Matthews.

Congratulations to Joann Warnett on being picked to represent Greater London in the All England Schools Cross-Country Championships at Lincoln. She won the Wandsworth Schools, finished 3rd in the Inner London and then 5th in the Greater London Championships.

It is nice to see Alison Bethwaite back in training after illness at Christmas.

Wendy Dunsford will be the Womens Captain for the coming year, and my Assistant Secretary will be Derrick Jones, who comes to help every Sunday.

Please come and support us when we compete at Battersea Park in the Southern League, Mid-Week League, and the youngsters in the Lily 'B' League. Your support means much to us, so please bring your Mums and Dads.

items.heading: MONEY MATTERS £
items.summary: Co-Auditor Ken Miller's A.G.M. statement on the club's finances, reporting a loss for the year to June 1977 and warning that Belgrave Harriers must improve its position by at least £1,000 a year.
items.text:
MONEY MATTERS £

At the A.G.M. last September Ken Miller, one of our co-Auditors incisively outlined the Club's financial position. The Committee regards it as important that all our members should be aware of the constant struggle to make ends meet and we therefore reproduce below Ken's comments.

"The Accounts for the year to 30th June 1977 show a loss of £663 of which £246 represents a provision for depreciation. There was thus a cash loss of £417. Apart from a very small deficit in 1975, this is the only occasion since before 1970 that the Club has suffered an outflow of cash. As explained by the Treasurer, the reason in part for this outflow, has been the restricted use of the Hall for social activities during the building programme.

The Balance Sheet at 30th June 1977 shows that after meeting our immediate liabilities, we have surplus cash of £867. Please remember this figure. But what of the future? If we assume that for the year to June 1978, expenditure will increase by 10%; subs. will be static[illegible] Building Society interest will reduce to a small figure; other income (football scheme, hire of hall, socials, etc.) will increase by £500 - the Club will have a cash loss of £500 for the year. But the position is worse than this, for we have already received £400 advance subscriptions. Thus our cash position will deteriorate by £900 during the current year on these assumptions. If we refer back to the fact that we had at June 1977 £867 surplus cash, we could find that the money has run out by next June.

But the problems do not stop at June 1978 for we have already received and effectively spent £400 of subscriptions for the year 1978/79.

A Club with the responsibility of a building such as Belgrave Hall, must in my view have some reserves upon which to fall back for major repairs. We have therefore not just to seek to cover our cash outgoings but also to cover a charge for depreciation to provide a build up of cash for this purpose. A sensible depreciation charge each year on the improved Belgrave Hall would be in the region of £350-£400.

To summarise, we need to improve the financial position of Belgrave Harriers by at least £1,000 per annum. This can only be achieved in two ways -

(1) Cutting costs (marginal scope)
(2) Increasing income - from socials, hire of hall, etc.
- from subscriptions.

Under the Rules of the Club, subscriptions cannot be increased until 1st July 1978 but it is interesting to note that currently subs. only just cover the cost of printing, stationery and postage (including the "Belgravian").

It is the Auditors' prime function to report on the past but my co-Auditor and I felt we would be failing in our duty if we did not underline this evening the potentially serious financial future facing the Club."

K.W. Miller.

items.heading: YOUTHS AND BOYS
items.byline: Leo Coy - Youths, Boys and Colts Secretary
items.summary: Youths and Boys secretary Leo Coy reviews a strong cross country season including the team's Surrey League victory, and outlines track plans in the Rosenheim and Ebbisham Leagues, an appeal for helpers and training times.
items.text:
YOUTHS AND BOYS

Cross Country Season.

After an initial shock over the resignation of Alan Perriam, who has moved north, the season proved to be one of our best for some years. Alan has already been greatly missed and we hope that he will return in the not too distant future.

The highlight of the season was our team victory in the Surrey League Our result at Wimbledon, like the Seniors, set us up for the rest of the season. This was our first win in any cross country race for a number of years and is an encouraging sign for the future. Of our scoring teams in the league only Richard Dorman won't be eligible for next year. So we intend to show the seniors again how it should be done by winning Div. I in 1978/9.

Another achievement was our good turnout in the Surrey Championships where we completed a team, despite a number of absentees in every age group. Next year with David North eligible to run for us we stand a great chance of being in the medals in the Youths race.

Our turnout in the HHH league at Brockwell Park was very disappointing. We could have won this if everybody had turned out. Hopefully we can improve next year.

Track Season.

The coming track season has a new feature in that we shall be competing in the Rosenheim League for the first time. There is a separate section for a youths team, with one scoring in each event and any number of non-scorers. The league is held over five matches with the first three teams going into the final.

The Boys/Colts will again be competing in the Ebbisham League but included for the first time are second year boys.

If any young athletes want to take part in the above leagues please see me at Battersea Park or give me a ring.

Note to older Members and Parents.

I still need help to run this section of the club. If you feel that you can help in any way please get in touch with me. The club has a better gathering of young athletes now than at any time before so it is up to everyone to make sure that they become the seniors of the future.

Training.

Club training sessions will be held on Sunday morning, Tuesday and Thursday evenings throughout the spring and early summer for all events.

Leo Coy - Youths, Boys and Colts Secretary (Tel: 01-764-8056).

items.text:
from the Belgravian...
... 25 years ago

COUNTY SENIOR C.C. CHAMPIONSHIPS......1953

These were held on 3rd January, and the Surrey event was in Richmond Park, which was more or less familiar ground to our team. We were not at full strength.....and did not expect to retain our team title, which we had held for the past two seasons. Our team, however, all ran well and we only lost first place by five points and second place by one point. Chas. Walker was our first man home in 5th position, then came Bill Lucas, 12th, and Bill only came into the team in order to make up the number, as he says he has retired from serious competition and declined an invitation to run in the Inter-Counties race. (Other members: 14.E.A. Short; 14.E.Herbert; 16.D.Brickwood; 21.J. Masters; 36.D.Briggs; 44.A.H.Bishop; 53.J.Bromley; 55.E.M.Bishop; 63.S.Davies; 67.L.C.Bishop; 74.G.J.Stace).

The Middlesex event was held at Trent Park and here again Cadogan AC were weakened.....and eventually placed 6th. Bob Taylor ran well to finish 20th, and Mick Porter 27th also did well. (Other members: 63.E.Stimpson; 70.J.McDonald; 73.R.W.Tobin; 85.R.J.Wolton; 127.A. Penstone; Ken Stimpson did not finish). Ed: a club was only allowed to compete in one county championship in those days so our Middlesex men had to run under the name of Cadogan AC - a second claim club whose membership was restricted to Belgravians.

items.heading: ... and 40 years ago: R.W.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS.......1938
items.summary: Reprint from 1938 celebrating Belgrave walkers' unprecedented treble of R.W.A. 'Junior' 10 miles, 20 miles and 50 km team titles, led by Colin Sutton, with the club holding all five R.W.A. trophies.
items.text:
... and 40 years ago

R.W.A. CHAMPIONSHIPS.......1938.

The accomplishment which must command our attention above all other matters, and merits our sincerest congratulation, is that of our walkers in winning the R.W.A. 10 miles "Junior" Championship, R.W.A. 20 Miles Championship and R.W.A. 50 Kilos. Championship. No other club has ever at any time won all three championships and to do so in the space of three months is almost miraculous. This record of success is one that may never again be approached by any club, and we most heartily congratulate and thank the members of the winning teams.

The performance of Colin Sutton in appearing in all three championship teams is one that may never be equalled. He was sixth in the "Junior", fourth in the 20 Miles Championship, and fifth in the 50 Kilos.Championship - a trio of performances that reflect the greatest credit on Colin's conscientious training and determined efforts to help the Club to a treble victory.

Others deserving our congratulations are Fred Bentley, who was placed second in both 20 Miles and 50 Kilos events; and Joe Coleman and Len Coleman, who dead-heated in the "Junior" Championship for first place.

It is interesting to note that as a result of the Winter season's activities, all five trophies which the Road Walking Association offer for competition (the "National" Shield, "Garnett" Cup, "Horlick" Cup, "Nijmegan" Shield and "Berman" Cup) are in the possession of Belgrave Harriers!

NOVEMBER 26th 1977 - PETERSHAM - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2).

A SECOND LEAGUE WIN

Meeting Ranelagh H on their home ground proved to be no problem for the Bels. even though four of our scorers from the previous race had other commitments on this day. DECEMBER 3rd 1977 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 7 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP.

IT'S THAT MAN AGAIN

Having scored a double during the summer with the 5,000 and 10,000 championships Laurie set about the first leg of the Club's winter championships with a fine Blackstaffe Shield victory. Our old Heathen friend and guest Bob Richardson scored over Colin Pearson and coming into form nicely to take the 'bronze' came Lionel Mann. If there was ever a vote for the youngster most Belgrave distance runn[illegible] would like to see succeed, Brian Marmion could well come out on top. Not endowed with a great deal in the way of natural ability he has stuck at it over the past few years, more often than not getting a hammering in the process. Brian successfully negotiated three laps of our course at a faster pace than he has usually taken in the past for just one circuit and in the process stormed off with the handicap prize.

DECEMBER 10th 1977 - CRYSTAL PALACE - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE (DIV 2).

BEATEN AT THE PALACE

A totally new course to us this one, with a much smaller lap than usual due to the fact that TV coverage was being given to the international race held on the same afternoon. With John Bicourt racing on the Continent it fell to Bob Richardson's lot to lead the Bels home. Our packing was not quite what it had been in the earlier two races. Ian Duncan was also absent, competing successfully in a University race, while Jim Rimmer seemed to have more than a little difficulty keeping his shorts on and even with second-claimer John Abberton of Poly H in our colours Ranelagh had no difficulty in beating us to the line. In fact half the first twenty men home were Ranelagh Harriers with only five Belgravians finished at that point. Luckily our next five runners were soon in and we still placed a comfortable second, maintaining an 80 point lead overall.

Pat O'Connor had the measure of Bill Weller on this occasion and it was good to see Bob Smith scoring for us again. Peter Gardner crept ever nearer the scorers being our 11th man and only 7 seconds down on Lionel Mann. Laurie O'Hara, meanwhile, finished with a personal score of 14 points after three races - just two down on the overall leader, Hutchin of Met. Police.

JANUARY 1st 1978 - CITY OF LONDON - 10 MILE ROAD RACE.

A Fine Start ....

.... was made to 1978. At 1.00 p.m. on New Year's Day in the City of London five Belgravians lined up for the seven lap course (starting and finishing in London Wall) for the Ten Miles Road Race, the first event of the City of London New Year Road Races. There were over 170 starters (including four ladies) and the team race was decided on aggregate times instead of positions, so every second was vital. JANUARY 14th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - BELGRAVE 10 MILE C.C. CHAMPIONSHIP.

LAURIE'S WINTER DOUBLE

At last it appeared that Laurie's time might be drawing to a close as Ian Duncan, less than half the master's age, stuck to him like glue for two laps and even ventured to match strides side by side on occasion. But Laurie was only toying with his young adversary and at the crucial stage on the third lap he put his foot down and it was all over; the winter 'double' was his. Colin Pearson, in dogging these two's footsteps early on, seemed to have the third spot sewn up but from about seven miles Bill Weller and then Leo Coy and Paul Roche seemed to be making ground on him. A hard fought last lap was to no avail and Bill came home 11 seconds ahead. Alan Painter was the deserving handicap winner but Steve Williams must also get a mention, finishing as he did cut, bruised and muddied from a very heavy fall on the horseride.

items.heading: FEBRUARY 18th 1978 - MILFORD - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE DIV.2. GOING UP!
items.summary: Report of the final Surrey Cross Country League Division 2 fixture at Milford, where Ranelagh won on the day but Belgrave won the division overall (final result table) and promotion back to Division I, with the Youths also winning their section.
items.text:
FEBRUARY 18th 1978 - MILFORD - SURREY C.C. LEAGUE DIV.2.

GOING UP!

A year ago we were bemoaning the fact that we had finished bottom of Division I of the N.Surrey League and would be relegated. "Only for a year" we said. On February 18th we travelled to Milford for the final fixture of the season. We were 80 points up on Ranelagh H and we knew that they were fielding a very strong team, so a keen race was expected. The course was over sandy paths over heathland; the recent weather had covered them with snow, making them slippery in places.

Our Youths had already shown their views on being in Division II by winning their section (they do not have as many races as the Seniors) Our hosts, Guildford & Godalming A.C.) had put on a race for them. David North scored a convincing win, with the improving Mark Sinclair fourth and in eighth position the diminutive Gary Williscroft. Later a blood-stained Ray McCann (he had had a fall) stormed in. Scoring three a side we won from the local club. Great running from great prospects, keep it up!

The Senior race, being over three laps, gave us a chance to assess our chances. Right from the first lap we had Ranelagh vests prominent in the first half dozen or so, with John Abberton in second place. Then Belgrave vests came through thick and fast and the necessary ten scorers, with a few to spare, were soon through. Second time round showed our team to be holding their positions, and so to the finish.

Ranelagh provided the winner, and with about a hundred yards to go John and another Ranelagh runner were neck and neck, but our man out sprinted his rival to gain a valuable place. The next three were solid Ranelagh, then Pat O'Connor led in a group containing many Belgrave vests. Particular mention for a newcomer from New Zealand (actually born in Britain), Lyn Jones whose forceful running split Lionel Mann and Jim Rimmer. Our scoring men, mostly "the old gang" were anchored by Steve Williams with Peter Hardwick and Simon Holmes hot on his heels - these three are soon going to worry our established seniors. It was pleasing to see Brian Marmion further up the field - let's hope he's on his way to showing his true potential.

A quick tot-up showed Ranelagh to have beaten us on the day's event, but they were well short of wiping out our initial advantage. So, next year it's Division I again, let's stay there! There was general elation as we got into the cars which sped us back home.

Finally, our thanks to the man whose efforts were largely responsible for our prowess - no, he didn't actually run, but he wrote to you, 'phoned you and conveyed some of you to the venue and got you to the start. Yes! Thank you Gordon Biscoe!

items.summary: Report of the National Cross Country Championships at Leeds, highlighting John Bicourt's 17th place from 1536 starters, with Belgrave senior and junior placings.
items.text:
MARCH 4th 1978 - LEEDS - E.C.C.U. CHAMPIONSHIPS.

A BICOURT "BLINDER"

It's Commonwealth Games and European Games year again and one may well have expected our most capped international John Bicourt to start to raise his game with a view to gaining selection for these championships later on this year. An early and promising result will have been noted by those who read every line of their "AWs" - February 2nd, Draguignan (France) 1.Boxberger, 2.J.Bicourt - but nobody could have forseen John's "blinder" of a run in this year's National. He travelled up to Leeds the day before the race in an effort to produce the most exciting cross country race of his career and succeeded magnificently. We have all heard how in the old days Belgrave used to pack them in, "all our team home in the first 30", etc. but let us remember that John's marvellous 17th place was from a field of 1536 starters, not the one or two hundred of the nineteen thirties. Runners finishing after him read like a list of who's who in English cross country: 18.A.Holden; 19.P.Standing; 22.R.Wilde; 23.D.Bedford; 27.K.Steer.....Crabb, Cannon, Beevor, Tagg....What a great pity that we did not turn out our best side to back him up and give ourselves a more respectable team place.

items.heading: MARCH 11th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE CHAMPIONSHIP. A NEW CHAMPION
items.summary: Report and results of the club 5¾ mile road championship at Wimbledon, won by Ian Duncan from Bill Weller, with handicap placings.
items.text:
MARCH 11th 1978 - WIMBLEDON - 5¾ MILE CHAMPIONSHIP

A NEW CHAMPION

It was a pleasant afternoon for the opening of our Spring road running season and by the end of the afternoon Team Manager Gordon Bisc[illegible] could at least pick out the likely candidates for "long-legs" in our Belgrave Road Relay.

After two miles Bill Weller and Ian Duncan, with Colin Pearson in their slipstream, had broken clear of the field and as they took the dip past the "Crooked Billet" Laurie O'Hara was a full 20 metres astern. Ian Duncan does not normally reckon to be a good hill runn[illegible] but as the field came into view again by the church after the mile long haul up Cambridge, Pepys and Cottenham Park Roads, he appeared to be edging ahead of Bill. Colin had gone back and although Lauri[illegible] appeared to be moving quite well it was obvious that on this day he was out of the hunt for victory.

Past the "Crooked Billet" again, and Bill Weller forced his way back to Ian's side; a mile round the top of the Common and still the issu[illegible] was not resolved. As the leading pair entered Lauriston Road for t[illegible] final straight an approaching car forced them to part, one on eithe[illegible] side, and at this point the younger man made his final effort to shake off our road running specialist, Bill Weller.

Ian broke clear at last, thereby gaining his first Club Championship less than a year inside becoming a member - congratulations!

The 2 miles race was one of the most exciting for a long time. Three runners, Jim Rimmer, Philip Joseph and Peter Gardner, raced neck and neck around the final turn having 'disposed' of decathlete Reg Hopkins 300 metres out. items.heading: ATHLETICS: A GROWTH INDUSTRY
items.summary: Humorous essay by Eric Hall, a former competitor and official now watching on television, on the growth of officials, commentators' clichés and support staff in athletics.
items.text:
ATHLETICS: A GROWTH INDUSTRY

As one who has competed, officiated and spectated but is now, alas confined by distance to tele bashing I have noticed some changes in the sport over the years. All my early experience of meetings was, I now realise, giving a surface impression. Now it is possible to see things in depth.

Some years ago at a fairly important meeting the centre of the arena was crowded with athletes, officials and hangers on - mainly the latter. The referee appealed for all non-essential personnel to leave the arena - no one moved. He repeated the appeal with the same result, he cajoled, he threatened but still after an hour or so it was the same - packed. It was the usual thing then. Get out in the middle and look important. However, during the mile the rains came. A cloudburst in fact and the result was just what the referee wanted - all but essential personnel left the arena. Not only left but rath[illegible] fled! Drowned! Only the scorers and timekeepers remained. The Almighty supported the referee.

Now all is different. A 22" picture (in colour naturally) of Crysta[illegible] Palace, Meadowbank or Cosford shows the crowds and we hear them described by Ron P., Stuart S., or Barry D., and next year ??? "The crowd numbers X thousand". "The crowd is knowledgeable" - that mea[illegible] they know how to get to Crystal Palace etc. "They are enthusiastic" that means not all have been able to get complimentary tickets. "They are right behind the team" or "the world record holder" or their "favourite" etc., and now "they are boosting them" or "lifting them" - that means the crowd are looking into the possibility of shipping them out by using man powered flight. Another source of fun is to try to spot the commentators word for the year. We have had "adrenalin" followed by "pain barrier" then came "fight back" and "long ha[illegible] season" but this year it has been "above themselves" and "world beaters" with the mind boggling "surpassing themselves" - this means you meet yourself coming back never having been.

Enough of the media and we have all had that I am sure. What about the centre of the arena? On a 22" screen it is still crowded. At times it outnumbers the crowd in the stands but in contrast to my earlier picture this time they are all essential. We now have carefully groomed, white trousered, white haired or balding officials carrying out a wide range of duties. I now spend some of the viewing time spotting old friends - Theo, Julian, Brutus - not their real names of course I have no wish to be sued! One we saw recently didn[illegible] move for well over an hour - he was either playing "Statues" or Madame Tussauds had done a damn good job! I digress, back to the officials - each man has his set duties, computer prepared and each vital to the success of the whole. To name them all would make for a paper shortage but I have selected those concerned with starting a race. We have spotted the starter, the deputy starter, the ammunition keeper, the assistant starter, the gun holder and deputy, the microphone holder, electrician and assistant plus deputies; the lane marshals, generals, majors and sergeants; the block carriers, but alas I have noticed the passing of the nail carriers and that most important official - the hammer holder - Tartan meant redundancy.

The proliferation of officials is not restricted to the meeting itself. Athletes need coaches, advisers, technical assistants, to say nothing of psychiatrists, psychologists, masseurs etc.etc. I have yet to actually see the jock strap carrier but there was a bloke with Litesome on his tracksuit at a recent meeting! In my day we had one piece of soap for the whole team but now I assume they each have their own and have a gold plated container.

The big question for the future is where will it end? You will recall that London hosts the Olympics every forty years and 1988 is not too far away. What the hell is the connection you ask? It should be apparent. By 1988 given the growth in the number of officials needed for a meeting and the decline in the population of London there will not be enough people in the area in 1988 to provide officials.

On a much more serious note though, they don't seem to need the same number of officials at foreign venues and they know when a world record has been broken too!

Eric Hall
